newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: SOCCER-COSTA RICA HAND UNITED STATES FIRST DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COSTA RICA HAND UNITED STATES FIRST DEFEAT.

text.p: Costa Rica beat the United States 2-1 on Sunday to hand the North Americans their first defeat of the World Cup qualifying competition.
Paulo Wanchope's opening goal for Costa Rica in the 39th minute was also the first the U.S. had conceded in a World Cup qualifier since a 2-1 win over Guatemala in 1989.
The result, in CONCACAF semi-final group one, left both teams needing a win from two games to make sure of a place in the final six-team round of the region's World Cup qualifying tournament.
Both teams, however, will go through in any case if Guatemala fail to beat Trinidad-Tobago on December 8.
Costa Rica, who reached the last 16 in 1990 on their only appearance in the World Cup finals, took the game to their opponents early on with a neat-short passing game.

Wanchope, the outstanding player of the field, nearly scored in the third minute while U.S. goalkeeper Brad Friedel was warned by the referee for time-wasting in the first half as his team appeared to be playing for a draw.
Hernan Medford, a survivor from 1990, was also inspirational for Costa Rica.

Wilmer Lopez scored Costa Rica's second in the 84th minute with Cobi Jones grabbing a last minute consolation for the U.S. after a goalmouth scramble. U.S coach Steve Sampson admitted, however, that his team had been outplayed.

Costa Rica - Erick Lonnis, Ronald Gonzalez, Luis Maron, Javier Delgado, Mauricio Soles, Wilmer Lopez, Oscar Ramirez, Ronald Gomez, Hernan Medford (Allan Oviedo, 77), Rolando Fonseca, Paulo Wanchope (Mauricio Wright, 88).

U.S. - Brad Friedel, Alexi Lalas, Eddie Pope, Paul Caligiuri, Ernie Stewart, John Harkes, Cobi Jones, Claudio Reyna, Preki Radosavijevic, (Mike Burns, 30), Eric Wynalda, Joe- Max Moore (Brian McBride, 74).
